To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1,25(OH)2D3-stimulates PKA activity, and PKA activity mediates calcium uptake in enterocytes.
the 1.25D3-MARS receptor mediates 1.25 D3-stimulated intestinal calcium uptake and the PKA pathway is the major pathway for this effect.
the 1 25D3-MARS (membrane-associated rapid response steroid-binding receptor) is essential for 1,25 D3-stimulated PK-A activation and calcium uptake in mouse enterocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium in intestinal epithelial cell function, and we are interested in the role of vitamin D and its receptor in the regulation of intestinal calcium uptake and calcium transport.
the mechanism by which the vitamin D receptor (VDR) mediates calcium uptake in intestinal cells.
the role of the ERp57/1,25D(3)-MARRS receptor in calcium uptake by enterocytes, and the mechanism(s) involved in its regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 1α,25(OH)2D3-MARRSR (membrane-associated rapid response steroid receptor) is of central importance in calcium uptake in mammal intestinal cells.

the targeted knockout of ERp57 in mice results in a blunted or absent response of intestinal cells to 1,25(OH)2D3, and that the 1alpha-hydroxylase knockout results in a blunting of the response of intestinal cells, and that the knockout of both genes results in an absence of response to 1, 25(OH)D3.
the 1.25D3-MARS receptor is of central significance to the rapid response of intestinal epithelial calcium transport to 1.25 D3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the 1, 25D3-MARS (Membrane Associated, Rapid Response Steroids Binding) receptor (PDIA3/ErP57) and that it is the major receptor for the hormone in intestinal cells.

the 1α-hydroxylase, the vitamin D receptor, and the 1, 25D3-Membrane Associated Rapid Response Steroid-Binding protein (MARRS) are all required for the rapid response of intestinal cells to 1,25(OH)2D3, and that the MARRS protein is the major mediator of the rapid response of enterocytes to 1, 2D3.
ERp57 is a critical component of the 1α,25(OH)2D3 receptor complex, and is essential for the rapid, nongenomic effects of this steroid hormone on calcium uptake in enterocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the 1.25D3-MARS receptor is of central import to 1.25 D3 stimulated calcium uptake in mammalians intestinal cells.
calcium uptake is not a good indicator of vitamin D action.
the 1α-hydroxylase is a critical enzyme that regulates calcium absorption in the intestine.
